record.title: INTRODUCTION.
record.subjects: Scholars ; Students ; Religion ; Ethics ; Education ; All Other Miscellaneous Schools and Instruction ; Educational Support Services ; Administration of Education Programs
record.abstract: The author introduces articles featured in this issue including the work of scholars which examines the philosophical frameworks undergirding the pedagogical practices used in the religious studies classroom and how these practices may be transformed so that they can help students apply what they have learned as they negotiate complex ethical situations outside the academe.

record.title: RECALLING OUR VOCATION: A CONVERSATION ABOUT TEACHING WITH MARK C. TAYLOR.
record.subjects: Education ; Universities & colleges ; United States ; All Other Miscellaneous Schools and Instruction ; Educational Support Services ; Administration of Education Programs ; Colleges, Universities, and Professional Schools ; Educators ; Higher education ; Taylor, Mark C. ; Kant, Immanuel, 1724-1804
record.abstract: An interview with U.S. educator and philosopher of religion Mark C. Taylor on the continuing relevance of pedagogy in the 21st century is presented. Taylor observes that the existing model for university, first conceived by German philosopher Immanuel Kant, is becoming obsolete with the increasing cost of higher education. However, he believes that liberal arts education is more valuable than ever since it allows students to learn more about cultures and traditions different from their own.

record.title: EDUCATION AS EVENT: A CONVERSATION WITH JOHN D. CAPUTO.
record.subjects: Education ; Universities & colleges ; Students ; Religion ; Administration of Education Programs ; Educational Support Services ; All Other Miscellaneous Schools and Instruction ; Colleges, Universities, and Professional Schools ; Caputo, John D.
record.abstract: An interview with theologian and philosopher of religion John D. Caputo is presented. Caputo proposes a new framework for education built on the concept of the "event," a philosophical term referring to the coming of something that can radically transform societies and institutions for the better or for worse, as an alternative to both the current information-driven model of the secular university and to the growing turn towards an approach that focuses on the religious formation of students.
record.contributors: CAPUTO, JOHN D. ; DICKINSON, T. WILSON

record.title: SILENCE, PRAYER, AND DESIRE IN PEDAGOGICAL PRACTICES: A CONVERSATION WITH SARAH COAKLEY.
record.subjects: Prayer ; Religious educators ; Erotica ; United States ; American theologians ; Coakley, Sarah, 1951- ; Steiner, George, 1929-
record.abstract: An interview with American theologian Sarah Coakley on how spiritual practices like silent prayer inform her pedagogical practice is presented. Coakley shares that while she tries to make time for silent prayer amidst her numerous teaching commitments, such practices must not be included as a requirement in theological courses. Citing George Steiner's comments on the eroticism inherent in the teacher-student relationship, she warns theology teachers to be on guard against self-aggrandizement.

record.title: ENGAGED PHILOSOPHY OF RELIGION.
record.subjects: Philosophy ; Transcendence (Philosophy) ; Reasoning ; Metaphysical cosmology ; Suffering
record.abstract: The author presents his reflections on the three classical philosophical problems concerned with transcendence, meaningless suffering, and cosmology in terms of an "engaged philosophy of religion". He differentiates engaged philosophy from idealist philosophy, claiming that the latter attempts to explain phenomena in terms of an absolute, abstract truth divorced from material reality, while the former seeks to cultivate ethical reasoning drawn from actual relations and interactions with life.

record.title: PERFORMING RELIGIOUSLY BETWEEN PASSION AND RESISTANCE.
record.subjects: Religion in literature ; Religious studies ; Shaffer, Peter, 1926-2016 ; Derrida, Jacques, 1930-2004 ; Schechner, Richard, 1934-
record.abstract: The author describes how the examination of the double bind of passion and resistance as performed in Peter Shaffer's play "Equus" can open up transformative pedagogical possibilities for the study of religion. He cites the performative theories of Jacques Derrida and Richard Schechner to explain how "Equus" dramatizes the complex imbrications of religious passions and critical resistances to them, especially as seen through the dynamic between its protagonists Alan Strang and Martin Dysart.

record.title: TEACHING WITH FEAR AND TREMBLING: THE TRIAL OF ABRAHAM, THE READER, AND THE PROFESSOR.
record.subjects: Students ; College teachers ; Education ; Educational Support Services ; Administration of Education Programs ; All Other Miscellaneous Schools and Instruction ; Fear & Trembling (Book : Kierkegaard) ; Kierkegaard, Søren, 1813-1855
record.abstract: The author suggests that teaching Danish philosopher Søren Kierkegaard's 1832 book "Fear and Trembling" in the religious studies classroom could help both professors and students withstand the tendency to want ready-made answers to philosophical problems, which obscures the processes in which these answers are reached. He notes that the struggle between faith and doubt depicted by Kierkegaard resists easy integration into classroom activities aimed at the accumulation of empirical facts.

record.title: SLOW READING: LEARNING IN THE TIME OF THE BODY.
record.subjects: Students ; Education ; All Other Miscellaneous Schools and Instruction ; Educational Support Services ; Administration of Education Programs ; Educators ; Teaching methods ; Classroom environment
record.abstract: The author calls attention to the fracturing of temporality caused by the distractions that go hand-in-hand with 21st century life, which she claims has had a detrimental impact on the ability of students to apply themselves to activities requiring close textual attention. Thus, she urges educators to adapt some of the practices of medieval monastic communities in the modern classroom by modeling to their students the pleasures involved in attending to texts in a focused yet sensual manner.

record.title: PSALM RECITATION AND POST-SECULAR TIME: AUGUSTINE, THE IPOD, AND PSALM 90.
record.subjects: Biblical scholars ; Memory ; Analogy ; Recitation (Education) ; Bible. Psalms
record.abstract: The author encourages Biblical scholars to take into closer consideration the traditions of recitation and reception of the Book of Psalms, especially Psalm 90, in order for them to gain a more nuanced understanding of how these psalms imagine the nature of time itself. He observes how the Psalms are an anthology arranged according to different traditions of recitation and practice, and adds that St. Augustine used psalm recitation as an analogy to describe the workings of time and memory.

record.title: HEXIS AND GRACE: THE FORMATION OF SOULS AT PORT ROYAL AND ELSEWHERE.
record.subjects: Grace (Theology) ; Salvation ; Soul ; Religious life of children ; Aristotle, 384-322 B.C. ; Pascal, Jacqueline
record.abstract: The author discusses how Aristotle's concept of hexis (commonly translated as "habit" or "disposition") and the doctrine of grace developed by St. Augustine, has influenced the writing of the "Rule for Children" a 17th-century treatise by Jacqueline Pascal, directress of the girls' school at the convent Port Royal des Champs. He explains that the pedagogical principles set forth in Pascal's Rule were aimed at cultivating children's souls so that they could persevere on the path of salvation.

record.title: PEDAGOGY AND RADICAL EQUALITY: RANCIÈRE'S IGNORANT SCHOOLMASTER.
record.subjects: Intellect ; Education ; Equality ; All Other Miscellaneous Schools and Instruction ; Educational Support Services ; Administration of Education Programs ; Ignorant Schoolmaster: Five Lessons in Intellectual Emancipation, The (Book) ; Rancière, Jacques, 1940-
record.abstract: The author discusses how the idea of intellectual emancipation developed in Jacques Rancière's book "The Ignorant Schoolmaster," and the concept of the brain's plasticity described by Catherine Malabou could serve as philosophical foundations for a radical pedagogy that takes as its starting point the intrinsic equality of human intelligence. He stresses the need for genuinely progressive teaching practices in a time when the commercialization of knowledge reinforces economic inequality.

record.title: THE INTELLIGENCE OF THE BOOK: THE RELIGIOUS STUDIES CLASSROOM AS TRANSLATION WORKSHOP.
record.subjects: Religious education ; Teachers ; Religious literature ; Students ; Rancière, Jacques, 1940-
record.abstract: The author describes how the ideas set forth by philosopher Jacques Rancière in his book "The Ignorant Schoolmaster," could provide the basis for an emancipatory framework of religious education. As an alternative to the traditional classroom setup in which the teacher serves as the supreme arbiter of a text's meaning, he proposes an image of the classroom as a translation workshop in which the teacher guides the student towards a more personal and creative engagement with religious texts.

record.title: THREE CLASSROOM READINGS OF 'ETHNOGRAPHIC PRACTICE' IN RELIGIOUS STUDIES.
record.subjects: Ethnology ; Material culture ; Other (Philosophy) ; Geertz, Clifford, 1926-2006 ; Certeau, Michel de, 1925-1986
record.abstract: The author looks at several models of ethnographic practices of fieldwork and writing and their possible contributions to religious studies. She notes that American anthropologist Clifford Geertz favored a cultural-interpretivist approach to ethnography, while French philosopher Michel de Certeau observes that the value of ethnographic writing lies in its re-inscription of alterity. She also mentions the "ethnography of things," which examines how material culture works to shape human activity.

record.title: BEYOND MORAL DEVELOPMENT: RE-THEORIZING ETHICAL PRACTICES IN SERVICE LEARNING.
record.subjects: Ethics ; Students ; Learning ; Service learning ; Ricœur, Paul, 1913-2005
record.abstract: The author calls for a re-conceptualization of the philosophical framework behind the pedagogical practice of service learning based on the theories of Paul Ricoeur, who emphasizes the role of narrative in the development of the ethical self. He argues that the preoccupation of most of the service learning literature with assessing the "moral development" of students does not sufficiently address the ethical challenges encountered by students in the very practice of service learning itself.

record.title: TEACHING FOR SOCIAL JUSTICE: CREATING A CONTEXT FOR TRANSFORMATION.
record.subjects: College students ; Brazil ; Transformative learning ; Experiential learning ; Active learning ; Freire, Paulo, 1921-1997
record.abstract: The author explains how she applies the principles of transformative pedagogy described in the writings of Brazilian educator Paulo Freire in teaching ethics to American college students. She relates that rather than striving to indoctrinate her students with her own values, she employs the spiral of theory and praxis to come up with experiential learning activities that will help them think about how their actions could have a positive or negative impact on the communities in which they live.

record.title: JESUS BEYOND CHRIST: ERRI DE LUCA AND THE "SELF AS STUMBLING BLOCK".
record.subjects: Philosophy ; Poetics ; Bible translating ; Old Testament ; New Testament ; De Luca, Erri
record.abstract: The author highlights how the act of translating the Bible has allowed Italian left-wing activist Erri de Luca to come into contact with an "I" who is a "stumbling-block over himself." She explains that although De Luca defines himself as a non-believer who initially rejected the New Testament as a deviation from the original Hebrew letter of the Old Testament, his personal reimagining of the life of Jesus gave him a new reference point for reflecting on his own philosophy and poetics.

record.title: Spheres, Volume One: Bubbles.

record.abstract: The article reviews the book "Spheres: Bubbles," Volume One, by Peter Sloterdijk, translated by Wieland Hoban.
